601.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 6
601.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Khang:: Do you think smart robots will replace humans in the future, Mai?
Mai:: I don't think so, Khang. Robots will assist us with dangerous and tedious jobs, but they cannot show emotions.
Khang:: What will your future home look like?
Mai:: It will be an eco-friendly villa powered by solar energy, with automatic gardens on the roof.
Khang:: That sounds wonderful! Will you have a domestic robot?
Mai:: Yes, a smart robot will clean floors, cook meals, and wash clothes.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Environmental pollution is one of the most critical challenges facing humanity today. To create a greener and healthier world, everyone should strictly practice the 3Rs rule: Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle. We should reduce our electricity and water consumption by turning off appliances when not in use. We should reuse glass jars, plastic boxes, and canvas shopping bags. Furthermore, recycling paper and plastic bottles saves valuable natural resources and prevents landfill overflow.

601.clozeText: Robots are becoming an indispensable part of modern society. Today, industrial robots work in automotive factories to assemble complex parts (23) ________ high precision. In healthcare, robotic surgical arms assist doctors in performing delicate operations safely. In the coming decades, domestic robots will enter millions of households. They (24) ________ take care of elderly people, water house plants, and tutor children in foreign (25) ________. However, scientists believe that robots will not completely replace human teachers (26) ________ robots lack genuine empathy and moral (27) ________.
601.readingText: Imagine living in a smart eco-house fifty years from now. These futuristic residences will be built from self-healing recycled materials and equipped with energy-generating solar glass windows. A central artificial intelligence system will manage the household, adjusting room temperatures and ambient music according to your mood. On the rooftop, automated hydroponic gardens will produce fresh organic vegetables all year round without requiring soil. Rainwater will be collected, filtered, and purified for daily consumption. Such houses will minimize environmental footprints and foster harmonious coexistence with nature.
601.passageText:
📖 ĐOẠN VĂN ĐIỀN TỪ (CLOZE TEXT - PART 4):
Robots are becoming an indispensable part of modern society. Today, industrial robots work in automotive factories to assemble complex parts (23) ________ high precision. In healthcare, robotic surgical arms assist doctors in performing delicate operations safely. In the coming decades, domestic robots will enter millions of households. They (24) ________ take care of elderly people, water house plants, and tutor children in foreign (25) ________. However, scientists believe that robots will not completely replace human teachers (26) ________ robots lack genuine empathy and moral (27) ________.

📖 ĐOẠN VĂN ĐỌC HIỂU (READING COMPREHENSION - PART 5):
Imagine living in a smart eco-house fifty years from now. These futuristic residences will be built from self-healing recycled materials and equipped with energy-generating solar glass windows. A central artificial intelligence system will manage the household, adjusting room temperatures and ambient music according to your mood. On the rooftop, automated hydroponic gardens will produce fresh organic vegetables all year round without requiring soil. Rainwater will be collected, filtered, and purified for daily consumption. Such houses will minimize environmental footprints and foster harmonious coexistence with nature.

601.sampleWritingText: In the future, I dream of living in a smart solar-powered villa on an ocean island. The house will be equipped with intelligent robots to handle all chores such as cooking, cleaning, and gardening. Large transparent solar panels will generate sufficient electricity, and an automatic rainwater filtration system will supply clean water. Living in such an eco-friendly house will keep me healthy and close to nature.

602.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 6
602.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Khang:: Do you think smart robots will replace humans in the future, Mai?
Mai:: I don't think so, Khang. Robots will assist us with dangerous and tedious jobs, but they cannot show emotions.
Khang:: What will your future home look like?
Mai:: It will be an eco-friendly villa powered by solar energy, with automatic gardens on the roof.
Khang:: That sounds wonderful! Will you have a domestic robot?
Mai:: Yes, a smart robot will clean floors, cook meals, and wash clothes.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Environmental pollution is one of the most critical challenges facing humanity today. To create a greener and healthier world, everyone should strictly practice the 3Rs rule: Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle. We should reduce our electricity and water consumption by turning off appliances when not in use. We should reuse glass jars, plastic boxes, and canvas shopping bags. Furthermore, recycling paper and plastic bottles saves valuable natural resources and prevents landfill overflow.

603.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 6
603.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Khang:: Do you think smart robots will replace humans in the future, Mai?
Mai:: I don't think so, Khang. Robots will assist us with dangerous and tedious jobs, but they cannot show emotions.
Khang:: What will your future home look like?
Mai:: It will be an eco-friendly villa powered by solar energy, with automatic gardens on the roof.
Khang:: That sounds wonderful! Will you have a domestic robot?
Mai:: Yes, a smart robot will clean floors, cook meals, and wash clothes.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Environmental pollution is one of the most critical challenges facing humanity today. To create a greener and healthier world, everyone should strictly practice the 3Rs rule: Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle. We should reduce our electricity and water consumption by turning off appliances when not in use. We should reuse glass jars, plastic boxes, and canvas shopping bags. Furthermore, recycling paper and plastic bottles saves valuable natural resources and prevents landfill overflow.

604.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 6
604.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Khang:: Do you think smart robots will replace humans in the future, Mai?
Mai:: I don't think so, Khang. Robots will assist us with dangerous and tedious jobs, but they cannot show emotions.
Khang:: What will your future home look like?
Mai:: It will be an eco-friendly villa powered by solar energy, with automatic gardens on the roof.
Khang:: That sounds wonderful! Will you have a domestic robot?
Mai:: Yes, a smart robot will clean floors, cook meals, and wash clothes.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Environmental pollution is one of the most critical challenges facing humanity today. To create a greener and healthier world, everyone should strictly practice the 3Rs rule: Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle. We should reduce our electricity and water consumption by turning off appliances when not in use. We should reuse glass jars, plastic boxes, and canvas shopping bags. Furthermore, recycling paper and plastic bottles saves valuable natural resources and prevents landfill overflow.

605.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 6
605.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Khang:: Do you think smart robots will replace humans in the future, Mai?
Mai:: I don't think so, Khang. Robots will assist us with dangerous and tedious jobs, but they cannot show emotions.
Khang:: What will your future home look like?
Mai:: It will be an eco-friendly villa powered by solar energy, with automatic gardens on the roof.
Khang:: That sounds wonderful! Will you have a domestic robot?
Mai:: Yes, a smart robot will clean floors, cook meals, and wash clothes.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Environmental pollution is one of the most critical challenges facing humanity today. To create a greener and healthier world, everyone should strictly practice the 3Rs rule: Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle. We should reduce our electricity and water consumption by turning off appliances when not in use. We should reuse glass jars, plastic boxes, and canvas shopping bags. Furthermore, recycling paper and plastic bottles saves valuable natural resources and prevents landfill overflow.

They (24) ________ take care of elderly people, water house plants, and tutor children in foreign (25) ________. However, scientists believe that robots will not completely replace human teachers (26) ________ robots lack genuine empathy and moral (27) ________.
605.readingText: Imagine living in a smart eco-house fifty years from now. These futuristic residences will be built from self-healing recycled materials and equipped with energy-generating solar glass windows. A central artificial intelligence system will manage the household, adjusting room temperatures and ambient music according to your mood. On the rooftop, automated hydroponic gardens will produce fresh organic vegetables all year round without requiring soil. Rainwater will be collected, filtered, and purified for daily consumption. Such houses will minimize environmental footprints and foster harmonious coexistence with nature.
605.passageText:
📖 ĐOẠN VĂN ĐIỀN TỪ (CLOZE TEXT - PART 4):
Robots are becoming an indispensable part of modern society. Today, industrial robots work in automotive factories to assemble complex parts (23) ________ high precision. In healthcare, robotic surgical arms assist doctors in performing delicate operations safely. In the coming decades, domestic robots will enter millions of households. They (24) ________ take care of elderly people, water house plants, and tutor children in foreign (25) ________. However, scientists believe that robots will not completely replace human teachers (26) ________ robots lack genuine empathy and moral (27) ________.

📖 ĐOẠN VĂN ĐỌC HIỂU (READING COMPREHENSION - PART 5):
Imagine living in a smart eco-house fifty years from now. These futuristic residences will be built from self-healing recycled materials and equipped with energy-generating solar glass windows. A central artificial intelligence system will manage the household, adjusting room temperatures and ambient music according to your mood. On the rooftop, automated hydroponic gardens will produce fresh organic vegetables all year round without requiring soil. Rainwater will be collected, filtered, and purified for daily consumption. Such houses will minimize environmental footprints and foster harmonious coexistence with nature.

The house will be equipped with intelligent robots to handle all chores such as cooking, cleaning, and gardening. Large transparent solar panels will generate sufficient electricity, and an automatic rainwater filtration system will supply clean water. Living in such an eco-friendly house will keep me healthy and close to nature.

606.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 6
606.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Khang:: Do you think smart robots will replace humans in the future, Mai?
Mai:: I don't think so, Khang. Robots will assist us with dangerous and tedious jobs, but they cannot show emotions.
Khang:: What will your future home look like?
Mai:: It will be an eco-friendly villa powered by solar energy, with automatic gardens on the roof.
Khang:: That sounds wonderful! Will you have a domestic robot?
Mai:: Yes, a smart robot will clean floors, cook meals, and wash clothes.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Environmental pollution is one of the most critical challenges facing humanity today. To create a greener and healthier world, everyone should strictly practice the 3Rs rule: Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle. We should reduce our electricity and water consumption by turning off appliances when not in use. We should reuse glass jars, plastic boxes, and canvas shopping bags. Furthermore, recycling paper and plastic bottles saves valuable natural resources and prevents landfill overflow.

607.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 6
607.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Khang:: Do you think smart robots will replace humans in the future, Mai?
Mai:: I don't think so, Khang. Robots will assist us with dangerous and tedious jobs, but they cannot show emotions.
Khang:: What will your future home look like?
Mai:: It will be an eco-friendly villa powered by solar energy, with automatic gardens on the roof.
Khang:: That sounds wonderful! Will you have a domestic robot?
Mai:: Yes, a smart robot will clean floors, cook meals, and wash clothes.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Environmental pollution is one of the most critical challenges facing humanity today. To create a greener and healthier world, everyone should strictly practice the 3Rs rule: Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle. We should reduce our electricity and water consumption by turning off appliances when not in use. We should reuse glass jars, plastic boxes, and canvas shopping bags. Furthermore, recycling paper and plastic bottles saves valuable natural resources and prevents landfill overflow.

608.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 6
608.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Khang:: Do you think smart robots will replace humans in the future, Mai?
Mai:: I don't think so, Khang. Robots will assist us with dangerous and tedious jobs, but they cannot show emotions.
Khang:: What will your future home look like?
Mai:: It will be an eco-friendly villa powered by solar energy, with automatic gardens on the roof.
Khang:: That sounds wonderful! Will you have a domestic robot?
Mai:: Yes, a smart robot will clean floors, cook meals, and wash clothes.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Environmental pollution is one of the most critical challenges facing humanity today. To create a greener and healthier world, everyone should strictly practice the 3Rs rule: Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle. We should reduce our electricity and water consumption by turning off appliances when not in use. We should reuse glass jars, plastic boxes, and canvas shopping bags. Furthermore, recycling paper and plastic bottles saves valuable natural resources and prevents landfill overflow.

609.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 6
609.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Khang:: Do you think smart robots will replace humans in the future, Mai?
Mai:: I don't think so, Khang. Robots will assist us with dangerous and tedious jobs, but they cannot show emotions.
Khang:: What will your future home look like?
Mai:: It will be an eco-friendly villa powered by solar energy, with automatic gardens on the roof.
Khang:: That sounds wonderful! Will you have a domestic robot?
Mai:: Yes, a smart robot will clean floors, cook meals, and wash clothes.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Environmental pollution is one of the most critical challenges facing humanity today. To create a greener and healthier world, everyone should strictly practice the 3Rs rule: Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle. We should reduce our electricity and water consumption by turning off appliances when not in use. We should reuse glass jars, plastic boxes, and canvas shopping bags. Furthermore, recycling paper and plastic bottles saves valuable natural resources and prevents landfill overflow.

610.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 6
610.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Khang:: Do you think smart robots will replace humans in the future, Mai?
Mai:: I don't think so, Khang. Robots will assist us with dangerous and tedious jobs, but they cannot show emotions.
Khang:: What will your future home look like?
Mai:: It will be an eco-friendly villa powered by solar energy, with automatic gardens on the roof.
Khang:: That sounds wonderful! Will you have a domestic robot?
Mai:: Yes, a smart robot will clean floors, cook meals, and wash clothes.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Environmental pollution is one of the most critical challenges facing humanity today. To create a greener and healthier world, everyone should strictly practice the 3Rs rule: Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle. We should reduce our electricity and water consumption by turning off appliances when not in use. We should reuse glass jars, plastic boxes, and canvas shopping bags. Furthermore, recycling paper and plastic bottles saves valuable natural resources and prevents landfill overflow.

611.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 6
611.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Khang:: Do you think smart robots will replace humans in the future, Mai?
Mai:: I don't think so, Khang. Robots will assist us with dangerous and tedious jobs, but they cannot show emotions.
Khang:: What will your future home look like?
Mai:: It will be an eco-friendly villa powered by solar energy, with automatic gardens on the roof.
Khang:: That sounds wonderful! Will you have a domestic robot?
Mai:: Yes, a smart robot will clean floors, cook meals, and wash clothes.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Environmental pollution is one of the most critical challenges facing humanity today. To create a greener and healthier world, everyone should strictly practice the 3Rs rule: Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle. We should reduce our electricity and water consumption by turning off appliances when not in use. We should reuse glass jars, plastic boxes, and canvas shopping bags. Furthermore, recycling paper and plastic bottles saves valuable natural resources and prevents landfill overflow.

612.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 6
612.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Khang:: Do you think smart robots will replace humans in the future, Mai?
Mai:: I don't think so, Khang. Robots will assist us with dangerous and tedious jobs, but they cannot show emotions.
Khang:: What will your future home look like?
Mai:: It will be an eco-friendly villa powered by solar energy, with automatic gardens on the roof.
Khang:: That sounds wonderful! Will you have a domestic robot?
Mai:: Yes, a smart robot will clean floors, cook meals, and wash clothes.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Environmental pollution is one of the most critical challenges facing humanity today. To create a greener and healthier world, everyone should strictly practice the 3Rs rule: Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle. We should reduce our electricity and water consumption by turning off appliances when not in use. We should reuse glass jars, plastic boxes, and canvas shopping bags. Furthermore, recycling paper and plastic bottles saves valuable natural resources and prevents landfill overflow.

613.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 6
613.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Khang:: Do you think smart robots will replace humans in the future, Mai?
Mai:: I don't think so, Khang. Robots will assist us with dangerous and tedious jobs, but they cannot show emotions.
Khang:: What will your future home look like?
Mai:: It will be an eco-friendly villa powered by solar energy, with automatic gardens on the roof.
Khang:: That sounds wonderful! Will you have a domestic robot?
Mai:: Yes, a smart robot will clean floors, cook meals, and wash clothes.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Environmental pollution is one of the most critical challenges facing humanity today. To create a greener and healthier world, everyone should strictly practice the 3Rs rule: Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle. We should reduce our electricity and water consumption by turning off appliances when not in use. We should reuse glass jars, plastic boxes, and canvas shopping bags. Furthermore, recycling paper and plastic bottles saves valuable natural resources and prevents landfill overflow.

614.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Khang:: Do you think smart robots will replace humans in the future, Mai?
Mai:: I don't think so, Khang. Robots will assist us with dangerous and tedious jobs, but they cannot show emotions.
Khang:: What will your future home look like?
Mai:: It will be an eco-friendly villa powered by solar energy, with automatic gardens on the roof.
Khang:: That sounds wonderful! Will you have a domestic robot?
Mai:: Yes, a smart robot will clean floors, cook meals, and wash clothes.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Environmental pollution is one of the most critical challenges facing humanity today. To create a greener and healthier world, everyone should strictly practice the 3Rs rule: Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle. We should reduce our electricity and water consumption by turning off appliances when not in use. We should reuse glass jars, plastic boxes, and canvas shopping bags. Furthermore, recycling paper and plastic bottles saves valuable natural resources and prevents landfill overflow.

615.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 6
615.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Khang:: Do you think smart robots will replace humans in the future, Mai?
Mai:: I don't think so, Khang. Robots will assist us with dangerous and tedious jobs, but they cannot show emotions.
Khang:: What will your future home look like?
Mai:: It will be an eco-friendly villa powered by solar energy, with automatic gardens on the roof.
Khang:: That sounds wonderful! Will you have a domestic robot?
Mai:: Yes, a smart robot will clean floors, cook meals, and wash clothes.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Environmental pollution is one of the most critical challenges facing humanity today. To create a greener and healthier world, everyone should strictly practice the 3Rs rule: Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle. We should reduce our electricity and water consumption by turning off appliances when not in use. We should reuse glass jars, plastic boxes, and canvas shopping bags. Furthermore, recycling paper and plastic bottles saves valuable natural resources and prevents landfill overflow.

616.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 6
616.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Khang:: Do you think smart robots will replace humans in the future, Mai?
Mai:: I don't think so, Khang. Robots will assist us with dangerous and tedious jobs, but they cannot show emotions.
Khang:: What will your future home look like?
Mai:: It will be an eco-friendly villa powered by solar energy, with automatic gardens on the roof.
Khang:: That sounds wonderful! Will you have a domestic robot?
Mai:: Yes, a smart robot will clean floors, cook meals, and wash clothes.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Environmental pollution is one of the most critical challenges facing humanity today. To create a greener and healthier world, everyone should strictly practice the 3Rs rule: Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle. We should reduce our electricity and water consumption by turning off appliances when not in use. We should reuse glass jars, plastic boxes, and canvas shopping bags. Furthermore, recycling paper and plastic bottles saves valuable natural resources and prevents landfill overflow.

617.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 6
617.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Khang:: Do you think smart robots will replace humans in the future, Mai?
Mai:: I don't think so, Khang. Robots will assist us with dangerous and tedious jobs, but they cannot show emotions.
Khang:: What will your future home look like?
Mai:: It will be an eco-friendly villa powered by solar energy, with automatic gardens on the roof.
Khang:: That sounds wonderful! Will you have a domestic robot?
Mai:: Yes, a smart robot will clean floors, cook meals, and wash clothes.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Environmental pollution is one of the most critical challenges facing humanity today. To create a greener and healthier world, everyone should strictly practice the 3Rs rule: Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle. We should reduce our electricity and water consumption by turning off appliances when not in use. We should reuse glass jars, plastic boxes, and canvas shopping bags. Furthermore, recycling paper and plastic bottles saves valuable natural resources and prevents landfill overflow.

618.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 6
618.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Khang:: Do you think smart robots will replace humans in the future, Mai?
Mai:: I don't think so, Khang. Robots will assist us with dangerous and tedious jobs, but they cannot show emotions.
Khang:: What will your future home look like?
Mai:: It will be an eco-friendly villa powered by solar energy, with automatic gardens on the roof.
Khang:: That sounds wonderful! Will you have a domestic robot?
Mai:: Yes, a smart robot will clean floors, cook meals, and wash clothes.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Environmental pollution is one of the most critical challenges facing humanity today. To create a greener and healthier world, everyone should strictly practice the 3Rs rule: Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle. We should reduce our electricity and water consumption by turning off appliances when not in use. We should reuse glass jars, plastic boxes, and canvas shopping bags. Furthermore, recycling paper and plastic bottles saves valuable natural resources and prevents landfill overflow.

619.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 6
619.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Khang:: Do you think smart robots will replace humans in the future, Mai?
Mai:: I don't think so, Khang. Robots will assist us with dangerous and tedious jobs, but they cannot show emotions.
Khang:: What will your future home look like?
Mai:: It will be an eco-friendly villa powered by solar energy, with automatic gardens on the roof.
Khang:: That sounds wonderful! Will you have a domestic robot?
Mai:: Yes, a smart robot will clean floors, cook meals, and wash clothes.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Environmental pollution is one of the most critical challenges facing humanity today. To create a greener and healthier world, everyone should strictly practice the 3Rs rule: Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle. We should reduce our electricity and water consumption by turning off appliances when not in use. We should reuse glass jars, plastic boxes, and canvas shopping bags. Furthermore, recycling paper and plastic bottles saves valuable natural resources and prevents landfill overflow.

620.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 6
620.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Khang:: Do you think smart robots will replace humans in the future, Mai?
Mai:: I don't think so, Khang. Robots will assist us with dangerous and tedious jobs, but they cannot show emotions.
Khang:: What will your future home look like?
Mai:: It will be an eco-friendly villa powered by solar energy, with automatic gardens on the roof.
Khang:: That sounds wonderful! Will you have a domestic robot?
Mai:: Yes, a smart robot will clean floors, cook meals, and wash clothes.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Environmental pollution is one of the most critical challenges facing humanity today. To create a greener and healthier world, everyone should strictly practice the 3Rs rule: Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle. We should reduce our electricity and water consumption by turning off appliances when not in use. We should reuse glass jars, plastic boxes, and canvas shopping bags. Furthermore, recycling paper and plastic bottles saves valuable natural resources and prevents landfill overflow.

701.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 7
701.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Mai:: What sources of energy will dominate our world in thirty years, Tom?
Tom:: I believe renewable energy like solar, wind, and tidal power will replace harmful fossil fuels.
Mai:: Why is transitioning to green energy so vital?
Tom:: Because fossil fuels produce greenhouse gas emissions that accelerate global warming and climate change.
Mai:: How will people travel in the future?
Tom:: We will likely travel in flying solar-powered cars and driverless magnetic levitation trains.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
New Zealand is an enchanting island country in the southwestern Pacific Ocean, consisting of two main landmasses: the North Island and the South Island. It is famous worldwide for its dramatic mountain ranges, pristine fjords, active geothermal volcanoes, and lush green meadows. The indigenous Maori culture forms an integral part of New Zealand's national identity, with distinctive traditions like the powerful Haka' dance and intricate tattoo art. The country is also renowned as the film location for the legendary Lord of the Rings' trilogy.

701.readingText: Australia is a unique continent and nation renowned for its striking biodiversity and natural wonders. Located between the Indian and Pacific Oceans, the country is home to eccentric wildlife found nowhere else on the planet, including marsupials like kangaroos, koalas, and the platypus. Off the northeastern coast of Queensland lies the Great Barrier Reef, the world's most extensive coral reef ecosystem, teeming with thousands of marine species. Australia's major coastal metropolises, notably Sydney and Melbourne, consistently rank among the most livable cities globally due to their high safety, vibrant cultural arts, and exceptional educational standards. However, climate change poses severe threats to Australia through intensifying bushfires and coral bleaching events.

702.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 7
702.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Mai:: What sources of energy will dominate our world in thirty years, Tom?
Tom:: I believe renewable energy like solar, wind, and tidal power will replace harmful fossil fuels.
Mai:: Why is transitioning to green energy so vital?
Tom:: Because fossil fuels produce greenhouse gas emissions that accelerate global warming and climate change.
Mai:: How will people travel in the future?
Tom:: We will likely travel in flying solar-powered cars and driverless magnetic levitation trains.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
New Zealand is an enchanting island country in the southwestern Pacific Ocean, consisting of two main landmasses: the North Island and the South Island. It is famous worldwide for its dramatic mountain ranges, pristine fjords, active geothermal volcanoes, and lush green meadows. The indigenous Maori culture forms an integral part of New Zealand's national identity, with distinctive traditions like the powerful Haka' dance and intricate tattoo art. The country is also renowned as the film location for the legendary Lord of the Rings' trilogy.

702.clozeText: Transitioning from depleting fossil fuels to sustainable clean energy is essential for combating climate change. Fossil fuels such as petroleum and coal currently supply the majority of global electricity, (23) ________ their combustion emits immense volumes of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere. This intensifies the global greenhouse effect and triggers catastrophic weather disasters. Fortunately, renewable alternatives like photovoltaic solar systems and offshore wind turbines are rapidly (24) ________ more efficient and affordable. Many industrialized nations are investing massively in green hydrogen infrastructure. By switching to renewable energy, humanity can ensure (25) ________ air quality, protect vulnerable natural ecosystems, and secure sustainable prosperity for future (26) ________ without compromising planetary (27) ________.
702.readingText: Australia is a unique continent and nation renowned for its striking biodiversity and natural wonders. Located between the Indian and Pacific Oceans, the country is home to eccentric wildlife found nowhere else on the planet, including marsupials like kangaroos, koalas, and the platypus. Off the northeastern coast of Queensland lies the Great Barrier Reef, the world's most extensive coral reef ecosystem, teeming with thousands of marine species. Australia's major coastal metropolises, notably Sydney and Melbourne, consistently rank among the most livable cities globally due to their high safety, vibrant cultural arts, and exceptional educational standards. However, climate change poses severe threats to Australia through intensifying bushfires and coral bleaching events.

703.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Mai:: What sources of energy will dominate our world in thirty years, Tom?
Tom:: I believe renewable energy like solar, wind, and tidal power will replace harmful fossil fuels.
Mai:: Why is transitioning to green energy so vital?
Tom:: Because fossil fuels produce greenhouse gas emissions that accelerate global warming and climate change.
Mai:: How will people travel in the future?
Tom:: We will likely travel in flying solar-powered cars and driverless magnetic levitation trains.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
New Zealand is an enchanting island country in the southwestern Pacific Ocean, consisting of two main landmasses: the North Island and the South Island. It is famous worldwide for its dramatic mountain ranges, pristine fjords, active geothermal volcanoes, and lush green meadows. The indigenous Maori culture forms an integral part of New Zealand's national identity, with distinctive traditions like the powerful Haka' dance and intricate tattoo art. The country is also renowned as the film location for the legendary Lord of the Rings' trilogy.

Fossil fuels such as petroleum and coal currently supply the majority of global electricity, (23) ________ their combustion emits immense volumes of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere. This intensifies the global greenhouse effect and triggers catastrophic weather disasters. Many industrialized nations are investing massively in green hydrogen infrastructure. By switching to renewable energy, humanity can ensure (25) ________ air quality, protect vulnerable natural ecosystems, and secure sustainable prosperity for future (26) ________ without compromising planetary (27) ________.
703.readingText: Australia is a unique continent and nation renowned for its striking biodiversity and natural wonders. Located between the Indian and Pacific Oceans, the country is home to eccentric wildlife found nowhere else on the planet, including marsupials like kangaroos, koalas, and the platypus. Off the northeastern coast of Queensland lies the Great Barrier Reef, the world's most extensive coral reef ecosystem, teeming with thousands of marine species. Australia's major coastal metropolises, notably Sydney and Melbourne, consistently rank among the most livable cities globally due to their high safety, vibrant cultural arts, and exceptional educational standards. However, climate change poses severe threats to Australia through intensifying bushfires and coral bleaching events.

704.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 7
704.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Mai:: What sources of energy will dominate our world in thirty years, Tom?
Tom:: I believe renewable energy like solar, wind, and tidal power will replace harmful fossil fuels.
Mai:: Why is transitioning to green energy so vital?
Tom:: Because fossil fuels produce greenhouse gas emissions that accelerate global warming and climate change.
Mai:: How will people travel in the future?
Tom:: We will likely travel in flying solar-powered cars and driverless magnetic levitation trains.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
New Zealand is an enchanting island country in the southwestern Pacific Ocean, consisting of two main landmasses: the North Island and the South Island. It is famous worldwide for its dramatic mountain ranges, pristine fjords, active geothermal volcanoes, and lush green meadows. The indigenous Maori culture forms an integral part of New Zealand's national identity, with distinctive traditions like the powerful Haka' dance and intricate tattoo art. The country is also renowned as the film location for the legendary Lord of the Rings' trilogy.

704.clozeText: Transitioning from depleting fossil fuels to sustainable clean energy is essential for combating climate change. Fossil fuels such as petroleum and coal currently supply the majority of global electricity, (23) ________ their combustion emits immense volumes of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere. This intensifies the global greenhouse effect and triggers catastrophic weather disasters. Fortunately, renewable alternatives like photovoltaic solar systems and offshore wind turbines are rapidly (24) ________ more efficient and affordable. Many industrialized nations are investing massively in green hydrogen infrastructure. By switching to renewable energy, humanity can ensure (25) ________ air quality, protect vulnerable natural ecosystems, and secure sustainable prosperity for future (26) ________ without compromising planetary (27) ________.
704.readingText: Australia is a unique continent and nation renowned for its striking biodiversity and natural wonders. Located between the Indian and Pacific Oceans, the country is home to eccentric wildlife found nowhere else on the planet, including marsupials like kangaroos, koalas, and the platypus. Off the northeastern coast of Queensland lies the Great Barrier Reef, the world's most extensive coral reef ecosystem, teeming with thousands of marine species. Australia's major coastal metropolises, notably Sydney and Melbourne, consistently rank among the most livable cities globally due to their high safety, vibrant cultural arts, and exceptional educational standards. However, climate change poses severe threats to Australia through intensifying bushfires and coral bleaching events.

705.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 7
705.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Mai:: What sources of energy will dominate our world in thirty years, Tom?
Tom:: I believe renewable energy like solar, wind, and tidal power will replace harmful fossil fuels.
Mai:: Why is transitioning to green energy so vital?
Tom:: Because fossil fuels produce greenhouse gas emissions that accelerate global warming and climate change.
Mai:: How will people travel in the future?
Tom:: We will likely travel in flying solar-powered cars and driverless magnetic levitation trains.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
New Zealand is an enchanting island country in the southwestern Pacific Ocean, consisting of two main landmasses: the North Island and the South Island. It is famous worldwide for its dramatic mountain ranges, pristine fjords, active geothermal volcanoes, and lush green meadows. The indigenous Maori culture forms an integral part of New Zealand's national identity, with distinctive traditions like the powerful Haka' dance and intricate tattoo art. The country is also renowned as the film location for the legendary Lord of the Rings' trilogy.

705.clozeText: Transitioning from depleting fossil fuels to sustainable clean energy is essential for combating climate change. Fossil fuels such as petroleum and coal currently supply the majority of global electricity, (23) ________ their combustion emits immense volumes of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere. This intensifies the global greenhouse effect and triggers catastrophic weather disasters. Fortunately, renewable alternatives like photovoltaic solar systems and offshore wind turbines are rapidly (24) ________ more efficient and affordable. Many industrialized nations are investing massively in green hydrogen infrastructure. By switching to renewable energy, humanity can ensure (25) ________ air quality, protect vulnerable natural ecosystems, and secure sustainable prosperity for future (26) ________ without compromising planetary (27) ________.
705.readingText: Australia is a unique continent and nation renowned for its striking biodiversity and natural wonders. Located between the Indian and Pacific Oceans, the country is home to eccentric wildlife found nowhere else on the planet, including marsupials like kangaroos, koalas, and the platypus. Off the northeastern coast of Queensland lies the Great Barrier Reef, the world's most extensive coral reef ecosystem, teeming with thousands of marine species. Australia's major coastal metropolises, notably Sydney and Melbourne, consistently rank among the most livable cities globally due to their high safety, vibrant cultural arts, and exceptional educational standards. However, climate change poses severe threats to Australia through intensifying bushfires and coral bleaching events.

706.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 7
706.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Mai:: What sources of energy will dominate our world in thirty years, Tom?
Tom:: I believe renewable energy like solar, wind, and tidal power will replace harmful fossil fuels.
Mai:: Why is transitioning to green energy so vital?
Tom:: Because fossil fuels produce greenhouse gas emissions that accelerate global warming and climate change.
Mai:: How will people travel in the future?
Tom:: We will likely travel in flying solar-powered cars and driverless magnetic levitation trains.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
New Zealand is an enchanting island country in the southwestern Pacific Ocean, consisting of two main landmasses: the North Island and the South Island. It is famous worldwide for its dramatic mountain ranges, pristine fjords, active geothermal volcanoes, and lush green meadows. The indigenous Maori culture forms an integral part of New Zealand's national identity, with distinctive traditions like the powerful Haka' dance and intricate tattoo art. The country is also renowned as the film location for the legendary Lord of the Rings' trilogy.

=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Mai:: What sources of energy will dominate our world in thirty years, Tom?
Tom:: I believe renewable energy like solar, wind, and tidal power will replace harmful fossil fuels.
Mai:: Why is transitioning to green energy so vital?
Tom:: Because fossil fuels produce greenhouse gas emissions that accelerate global warming and climate change.
Mai:: How will people travel in the future?
Tom:: We will likely travel in flying solar-powered cars and driverless magnetic levitation trains.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
New Zealand is an enchanting island country in the southwestern Pacific Ocean, consisting of two main landmasses: the North Island and the South Island. It is famous worldwide for its dramatic mountain ranges, pristine fjords, active geothermal volcanoes, and lush green meadows. The indigenous Maori culture forms an integral part of New Zealand's national identity, with distinctive traditions like the powerful Haka' dance and intricate tattoo art. The country is also renowned as the film location for the legendary Lord of the Rings' trilogy.

708.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 7
708.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Mai:: What sources of energy will dominate our world in thirty years, Tom?
Tom:: I believe renewable energy like solar, wind, and tidal power will replace harmful fossil fuels.
Mai:: Why is transitioning to green energy so vital?
Tom:: Because fossil fuels produce greenhouse gas emissions that accelerate global warming and climate change.
Mai:: How will people travel in the future?
Tom:: We will likely travel in flying solar-powered cars and driverless magnetic levitation trains.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
New Zealand is an enchanting island country in the southwestern Pacific Ocean, consisting of two main landmasses: the North Island and the South Island. It is famous worldwide for its dramatic mountain ranges, pristine fjords, active geothermal volcanoes, and lush green meadows. The indigenous Maori culture forms an integral part of New Zealand's national identity, with distinctive traditions like the powerful Haka' dance and intricate tattoo art. The country is also renowned as the film location for the legendary Lord of the Rings' trilogy.

708.clozeText: Transitioning from depleting fossil fuels to sustainable clean energy is essential for combating climate change. Fossil fuels such as petroleum and coal currently supply the majority of global electricity, (23) ________ their combustion emits immense volumes of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere. This intensifies the global greenhouse effect and triggers catastrophic weather disasters. Fortunately, renewable alternatives like photovoltaic solar systems and offshore wind turbines are rapidly (24) ________ more efficient and affordable. Many industrialized nations are investing massively in green hydrogen infrastructure. By switching to renewable energy, humanity can ensure (25) ________ air quality, protect vulnerable natural ecosystems, and secure sustainable prosperity for future (26) ________ without compromising planetary (27) ________.
708.readingText: Australia is a unique continent and nation renowned for its striking biodiversity and natural wonders. Located between the Indian and Pacific Oceans, the country is home to eccentric wildlife found nowhere else on the planet, including marsupials like kangaroos, koalas, and the platypus. Off the northeastern coast of Queensland lies the Great Barrier Reef, the world's most extensive coral reef ecosystem, teeming with thousands of marine species. Australia's major coastal metropolises, notably Sydney and Melbourne, consistently rank among the most livable cities globally due to their high safety, vibrant cultural arts, and exceptional educational standards. However, climate change poses severe threats to Australia through intensifying bushfires and coral bleaching events.

709.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 7
709.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Mai:: What sources of energy will dominate our world in thirty years, Tom?
Tom:: I believe renewable energy like solar, wind, and tidal power will replace harmful fossil fuels.
Mai:: Why is transitioning to green energy so vital?
Tom:: Because fossil fuels produce greenhouse gas emissions that accelerate global warming and climate change.
Mai:: How will people travel in the future?
Tom:: We will likely travel in flying solar-powered cars and driverless magnetic levitation trains.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
New Zealand is an enchanting island country in the southwestern Pacific Ocean, consisting of two main landmasses: the North Island and the South Island. It is famous worldwide for its dramatic mountain ranges, pristine fjords, active geothermal volcanoes, and lush green meadows. The indigenous Maori culture forms an integral part of New Zealand's national identity, with distinctive traditions like the powerful Haka' dance and intricate tattoo art. The country is also renowned as the film location for the legendary Lord of the Rings' trilogy.

709.clozeText: Transitioning from depleting fossil fuels to sustainable clean energy is essential for combating climate change. Fossil fuels such as petroleum and coal currently supply the majority of global electricity, (23) ________ their combustion emits immense volumes of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere. This intensifies the global greenhouse effect and triggers catastrophic weather disasters. Fortunately, renewable alternatives like photovoltaic solar systems and offshore wind turbines are rapidly (24) ________ more efficient and affordable. Many industrialized nations are investing massively in green hydrogen infrastructure. By switching to renewable energy, humanity can ensure (25) ________ air quality, protect vulnerable natural ecosystems, and secure sustainable prosperity for future (26) ________ without compromising planetary (27) ________.
709.readingText: Australia is a unique continent and nation renowned for its striking biodiversity and natural wonders. Located between the Indian and Pacific Oceans, the country is home to eccentric wildlife found nowhere else on the planet, including marsupials like kangaroos, koalas, and the platypus. Off the northeastern coast of Queensland lies the Great Barrier Reef, the world's most extensive coral reef ecosystem, teeming with thousands of marine species. Australia's major coastal metropolises, notably Sydney and Melbourne, consistently rank among the most livable cities globally due to their high safety, vibrant cultural arts, and exceptional educational standards. However, climate change poses severe threats to Australia through intensifying bushfires and coral bleaching events.

710.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 7
710.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Mai:: What sources of energy will dominate our world in thirty years, Tom?
Tom:: I believe renewable energy like solar, wind, and tidal power will replace harmful fossil fuels.
Mai:: Why is transitioning to green energy so vital?
Tom:: Because fossil fuels produce greenhouse gas emissions that accelerate global warming and climate change.
Mai:: How will people travel in the future?
Tom:: We will likely travel in flying solar-powered cars and driverless magnetic levitation trains.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
New Zealand is an enchanting island country in the southwestern Pacific Ocean, consisting of two main landmasses: the North Island and the South Island. It is famous worldwide for its dramatic mountain ranges, pristine fjords, active geothermal volcanoes, and lush green meadows. The indigenous Maori culture forms an integral part of New Zealand's national identity, with distinctive traditions like the powerful Haka' dance and intricate tattoo art. The country is also renowned as the film location for the legendary Lord of the Rings' trilogy.

710.readingText: Australia is a unique continent and nation renowned for its striking biodiversity and natural wonders. Located between the Indian and Pacific Oceans, the country is home to eccentric wildlife found nowhere else on the planet, including marsupials like kangaroos, koalas, and the platypus. Off the northeastern coast of Queensland lies the Great Barrier Reef, the world's most extensive coral reef ecosystem, teeming with thousands of marine species. Australia's major coastal metropolises, notably Sydney and Melbourne, consistently rank among the most livable cities globally due to their high safety, vibrant cultural arts, and exceptional educational standards. However, climate change poses severe threats to Australia through intensifying bushfires and coral bleaching events.

711.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 7
711.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Mai:: What sources of energy will dominate our world in thirty years, Tom?
Tom:: I believe renewable energy like solar, wind, and tidal power will replace harmful fossil fuels.
Mai:: Why is transitioning to green energy so vital?
Tom:: Because fossil fuels produce greenhouse gas emissions that accelerate global warming and climate change.
Mai:: How will people travel in the future?
Tom:: We will likely travel in flying solar-powered cars and driverless magnetic levitation trains.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===

712.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 7
712.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Mai:: What sources of energy will dominate our world in thirty years, Tom?
Tom:: I believe renewable energy like solar, wind, and tidal power will replace harmful fossil fuels.
Mai:: Why is transitioning to green energy so vital?
Tom:: Because fossil fuels produce greenhouse gas emissions that accelerate global warming and climate change.
Mai:: How will people travel in the future?
Tom:: We will likely travel in flying solar-powered cars and driverless magnetic levitation trains.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
New Zealand is an enchanting island country in the southwestern Pacific Ocean, consisting of two main landmasses: the North Island and the South Island. It is famous worldwide for its dramatic mountain ranges, pristine fjords, active geothermal volcanoes, and lush green meadows. The indigenous Maori culture forms an integral part of New Zealand's national identity, with distinctive traditions like the powerful Haka' dance and intricate tattoo art. The country is also renowned as the film location for the legendary Lord of the Rings' trilogy.

Fossil fuels such as petroleum and coal currently supply the majority of global electricity, (23) ________ their combustion emits immense volumes of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere. This intensifies the global greenhouse effect and triggers catastrophic weather disasters. Many industrialized nations are investing massively in green hydrogen infrastructure. By switching to renewable energy, humanity can ensure (25) ________ air quality, protect vulnerable natural ecosystems, and secure sustainable prosperity for future (26) ________ without compromising planetary (27) ________.
712.readingText: Australia is a unique continent and nation renowned for its striking biodiversity and natural wonders. Located between the Indian and Pacific Oceans, the country is home to eccentric wildlife found nowhere else on the planet, including marsupials like kangaroos, koalas, and the platypus. Off the northeastern coast of Queensland lies the Great Barrier Reef, the world's most extensive coral reef ecosystem, teeming with thousands of marine species. Australia's major coastal metropolises, notably Sydney and Melbourne, consistently rank among the most livable cities globally due to their high safety, vibrant cultural arts, and exceptional educational standards. However, climate change poses severe threats to Australia through intensifying bushfires and coral bleaching events.

713.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 7
713.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Mai:: What sources of energy will dominate our world in thirty years, Tom?
Tom:: I believe renewable energy like solar, wind, and tidal power will replace harmful fossil fuels.
Mai:: Why is transitioning to green energy so vital?
Tom:: Because fossil fuels produce greenhouse gas emissions that accelerate global warming and climate change.
Mai:: How will people travel in the future?
Tom:: We will likely travel in flying solar-powered cars and driverless magnetic levitation trains.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
New Zealand is an enchanting island country in the southwestern Pacific Ocean, consisting of two main landmasses: the North Island and the South Island. It is famous worldwide for its dramatic mountain ranges, pristine fjords, active geothermal volcanoes, and lush green meadows. The indigenous Maori culture forms an integral part of New Zealand's national identity, with distinctive traditions like the powerful Haka' dance and intricate tattoo art. The country is also renowned as the film location for the legendary Lord of the Rings' trilogy.

713.clozeText: Transitioning from depleting fossil fuels to sustainable clean energy is essential for combating climate change. Fossil fuels such as petroleum and coal currently supply the majority of global electricity, (23) ________ their combustion emits immense volumes of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere. This intensifies the global greenhouse effect and triggers catastrophic weather disasters. Fortunately, renewable alternatives like photovoltaic solar systems and offshore wind turbines are rapidly (24) ________ more efficient and affordable. Many industrialized nations are investing massively in green hydrogen infrastructure. By switching to renewable energy, humanity can ensure (25) ________ air quality, protect vulnerable natural ecosystems, and secure sustainable prosperity for future (26) ________ without compromising planetary (27) ________.
713.readingText: Australia is a unique continent and nation renowned for its striking biodiversity and natural wonders. Located between the Indian and Pacific Oceans, the country is home to eccentric wildlife found nowhere else on the planet, including marsupials like kangaroos, koalas, and the platypus. Off the northeastern coast of Queensland lies the Great Barrier Reef, the world's most extensive coral reef ecosystem, teeming with thousands of marine species. Australia's major coastal metropolises, notably Sydney and Melbourne, consistently rank among the most livable cities globally due to their high safety, vibrant cultural arts, and exceptional educational standards. However, climate change poses severe threats to Australia through intensifying bushfires and coral bleaching events.

714.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 7
714.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Mai:: What sources of energy will dominate our world in thirty years, Tom?
Tom:: I believe renewable energy like solar, wind, and tidal power will replace harmful fossil fuels.
Mai:: Why is transitioning to green energy so vital?
Tom:: Because fossil fuels produce greenhouse gas emissions that accelerate global warming and climate change.
Mai:: How will people travel in the future?
Tom:: We will likely travel in flying solar-powered cars and driverless magnetic levitation trains.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
New Zealand is an enchanting island country in the southwestern Pacific Ocean, consisting of two main landmasses: the North Island and the South Island. It is famous worldwide for its dramatic mountain ranges, pristine fjords, active geothermal volcanoes, and lush green meadows. The indigenous Maori culture forms an integral part of New Zealand's national identity, with distinctive traditions like the powerful Haka' dance and intricate tattoo art. The country is also renowned as the film location for the legendary Lord of the Rings' trilogy.

714.readingText: Australia is a unique continent and nation renowned for its striking biodiversity and natural wonders. Located between the Indian and Pacific Oceans, the country is home to eccentric wildlife found nowhere else on the planet, including marsupials like kangaroos, koalas, and the platypus. Off the northeastern coast of Queensland lies the Great Barrier Reef, the world's most extensive coral reef ecosystem, teeming with thousands of marine species. Australia's major coastal metropolises, notably Sydney and Melbourne, consistently rank among the most livable cities globally due to their high safety, vibrant cultural arts, and exceptional educational standards. However, climate change poses severe threats to Australia through intensifying bushfires and coral bleaching events.

715.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 7
715.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Mai:: What sources of energy will dominate our world in thirty years, Tom?
Tom:: I believe renewable energy like solar, wind, and tidal power will replace harmful fossil fuels.
Mai:: Why is transitioning to green energy so vital?
Tom:: Because fossil fuels produce greenhouse gas emissions that accelerate global warming and climate change.
Mai:: How will people travel in the future?
Tom:: We will likely travel in flying solar-powered cars and driverless magnetic levitation trains.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
New Zealand is an enchanting island country in the southwestern Pacific Ocean, consisting of two main landmasses: the North Island and the South Island. It is famous worldwide for its dramatic mountain ranges, pristine fjords, active geothermal volcanoes, and lush green meadows. The indigenous Maori culture forms an integral part of New Zealand's national identity, with distinctive traditions like the powerful Haka' dance and intricate tattoo art. The country is also renowned as the film location for the legendary Lord of the Rings' trilogy.

716.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 7
716.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Mai:: What sources of energy will dominate our world in thirty years, Tom?
Tom:: I believe renewable energy like solar, wind, and tidal power will replace harmful fossil fuels.
Mai:: Why is transitioning to green energy so vital?
Tom:: Because fossil fuels produce greenhouse gas emissions that accelerate global warming and climate change.
Mai:: How will people travel in the future?
Tom:: We will likely travel in flying solar-powered cars and driverless magnetic levitation trains.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
New Zealand is an enchanting island country in the southwestern Pacific Ocean, consisting of two main landmasses: the North Island and the South Island. It is famous worldwide for its dramatic mountain ranges, pristine fjords, active geothermal volcanoes, and lush green meadows. The indigenous Maori culture forms an integral part of New Zealand's national identity, with distinctive traditions like the powerful Haka' dance and intricate tattoo art. The country is also renowned as the film location for the legendary Lord of the Rings' trilogy.

By switching to renewable energy, humanity can ensure (25) ________ air quality, protect vulnerable natural ecosystems, and secure sustainable prosperity for future (26) ________ without compromising planetary (27) ________.
716.readingText: Australia is a unique continent and nation renowned for its striking biodiversity and natural wonders. Located between the Indian and Pacific Oceans, the country is home to eccentric wildlife found nowhere else on the planet, including marsupials like kangaroos, koalas, and the platypus. Off the northeastern coast of Queensland lies the Great Barrier Reef, the world's most extensive coral reef ecosystem, teeming with thousands of marine species. Australia's major coastal metropolises, notably Sydney and Melbourne, consistently rank among the most livable cities globally due to their high safety, vibrant cultural arts, and exceptional educational standards. However, climate change poses severe threats to Australia through intensifying bushfires and coral bleaching events.

717.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 7
717.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Mai:: What sources of energy will dominate our world in thirty years, Tom?
Tom:: I believe renewable energy like solar, wind, and tidal power will replace harmful fossil fuels.
Mai:: Why is transitioning to green energy so vital?
Tom:: Because fossil fuels produce greenhouse gas emissions that accelerate global warming and climate change.
Mai:: How will people travel in the future?
Tom:: We will likely travel in flying solar-powered cars and driverless magnetic levitation trains.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
New Zealand is an enchanting island country in the southwestern Pacific Ocean, consisting of two main landmasses: the North Island and the South Island. It is famous worldwide for its dramatic mountain ranges, pristine fjords, active geothermal volcanoes, and lush green meadows. The indigenous Maori culture forms an integral part of New Zealand's national identity, with distinctive traditions like the powerful Haka' dance and intricate tattoo art. The country is also renowned as the film location for the legendary Lord of the Rings' trilogy.

Fossil fuels such as petroleum and coal currently supply the majority of global electricity, (23) ________ their combustion emits immense volumes of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere. This intensifies the global greenhouse effect and triggers catastrophic weather disasters. Fortunately, renewable alternatives like photovoltaic solar systems and offshore wind turbines are rapidly (24) ________ more efficient and affordable. Many industrialized nations are investing massively in green hydrogen infrastructure. By switching to renewable energy, humanity can ensure (25) ________ air quality, protect vulnerable natural ecosystems, and secure sustainable prosperity for future (26) ________ without compromising planetary (27) ________.
717.readingText: Australia is a unique continent and nation renowned for its striking biodiversity and natural wonders. Located between the Indian and Pacific Oceans, the country is home to eccentric wildlife found nowhere else on the planet, including marsupials like kangaroos, koalas, and the platypus. Off the northeastern coast of Queensland lies the Great Barrier Reef, the world's most extensive coral reef ecosystem, teeming with thousands of marine species. Australia's major coastal metropolises, notably Sydney and Melbourne, consistently rank among the most livable cities globally due to their high safety, vibrant cultural arts, and exceptional educational standards. However, climate change poses severe threats to Australia through intensifying bushfires and coral bleaching events.

718.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 7
718.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Mai:: What sources of energy will dominate our world in thirty years, Tom?
Tom:: I believe renewable energy like solar, wind, and tidal power will replace harmful fossil fuels.
Mai:: Why is transitioning to green energy so vital?
Tom:: Because fossil fuels produce greenhouse gas emissions that accelerate global warming and climate change.
Mai:: How will people travel in the future?
Tom:: We will likely travel in flying solar-powered cars and driverless magnetic levitation trains.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
New Zealand is an enchanting island country in the southwestern Pacific Ocean, consisting of two main landmasses: the North Island and the South Island. It is famous worldwide for its dramatic mountain ranges, pristine fjords, active geothermal volcanoes, and lush green meadows. The indigenous Maori culture forms an integral part of New Zealand's national identity, with distinctive traditions like the powerful Haka' dance and intricate tattoo art. The country is also renowned as the film location for the legendary Lord of the Rings' trilogy.

718.clozeText: Transitioning from depleting fossil fuels to sustainable clean energy is essential for combating climate change. Fossil fuels such as petroleum and coal currently supply the majority of global electricity, (23) ________ their combustion emits immense volumes of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere. This intensifies the global greenhouse effect and triggers catastrophic weather disasters. Fortunately, renewable alternatives like photovoltaic solar systems and offshore wind turbines are rapidly (24) ________ more efficient and affordable. Many industrialized nations are investing massively in green hydrogen infrastructure. By switching to renewable energy, humanity can ensure (25) ________ air quality, protect vulnerable natural ecosystems, and secure sustainable prosperity for future (26) ________ without compromising planetary (27) ________.
718.readingText: Australia is a unique continent and nation renowned for its striking biodiversity and natural wonders. Located between the Indian and Pacific Oceans, the country is home to eccentric wildlife found nowhere else on the planet, including marsupials like kangaroos, koalas, and the platypus. Off the northeastern coast of Queensland lies the Great Barrier Reef, the world's most extensive coral reef ecosystem, teeming with thousands of marine species. Australia's major coastal metropolises, notably Sydney and Melbourne, consistently rank among the most livable cities globally due to their high safety, vibrant cultural arts, and exceptional educational standards. However, climate change poses severe threats to Australia through intensifying bushfires and coral bleaching events.

719.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Mai:: What sources of energy will dominate our world in thirty years, Tom?
Tom:: I believe renewable energy like solar, wind, and tidal power will replace harmful fossil fuels.
Mai:: Why is transitioning to green energy so vital?
Tom:: Because fossil fuels produce greenhouse gas emissions that accelerate global warming and climate change.
Mai:: How will people travel in the future?
Tom:: We will likely travel in flying solar-powered cars and driverless magnetic levitation trains.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
New Zealand is an enchanting island country in the southwestern Pacific Ocean, consisting of two main landmasses: the North Island and the South Island. It is famous worldwide for its dramatic mountain ranges, pristine fjords, active geothermal volcanoes, and lush green meadows. The indigenous Maori culture forms an integral part of New Zealand's national identity, with distinctive traditions like the powerful Haka' dance and intricate tattoo art. The country is also renowned as the film location for the legendary Lord of the Rings' trilogy.

Australia's major coastal metropolises, notably Sydney and Melbourne, consistently rank among the most livable cities globally due to their high safety, vibrant cultural arts, and exceptional educational standards. 720.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ CUỐI HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 7
720.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Mai:: What sources of energy will dominate our world in thirty years, Tom?
Tom:: I believe renewable energy like solar, wind, and tidal power will replace harmful fossil fuels.
Mai:: Why is transitioning to green energy so vital?
Tom:: Because fossil fuels produce greenhouse gas emissions that accelerate global warming and climate change.
Mai:: How will people travel in the future?
Tom:: We will likely travel in flying solar-powered cars and driverless magnetic levitation trains.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
New Zealand is an enchanting island country in the southwestern Pacific Ocean, consisting of two main landmasses: the North Island and the South Island. It is famous worldwide for its dramatic mountain ranges, pristine fjords, active geothermal volcanoes, and lush green meadows. The indigenous Maori culture forms an integral part of New Zealand's national identity, with distinctive traditions like the powerful Haka' dance and intricate tattoo art. The country is also renowned as the film location for the legendary Lord of the Rings' trilogy.

720.readingText: Australia is a unique continent and nation renowned for its striking biodiversity and natural wonders. Located between the Indian and Pacific Oceans, the country is home to eccentric wildlife found nowhere else on the planet, including marsupials like kangaroos, koalas, and the platypus. Off the northeastern coast of Queensland lies the Great Barrier Reef, the world's most extensive coral reef ecosystem, teeming with thousands of marine species. Australia's major coastal metropolises, notably Sydney and Melbourne, consistently rank among the most livable cities globally due to their high safety, vibrant cultural arts, and exceptional educational standards. However, climate change poses severe threats to Australia through intensifying bushfires and coral bleaching events.

801.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Minh:: Do you believe humans will discover extraterrestrial microbial life on Mars, Phong?
Phong:: Scientists say that robotic rovers on Mars have detected subsurface water and organic compounds, so microbial existence might be plausible.
Minh:: How will technological inventions reshape our everyday communication in fifty years?
Phong:: We might communicate via real-time three-dimensional holographic projections instead of handheld video screens.
Minh:: Will language barriers completely dissolve?
Phong:: Certainly! Implantable neural translation earbuds will translate spoken languages instantaneously into your native tongue.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Artificial intelligence and autonomous robotic systems are ushering in the Fourth Industrial Revolution, fundamentally transforming healthcare, manufacturing, and exploratory science. In cutting-edge hospitals, machine-learning algorithms analyze radiological scans to detect early-stage malignant tumors with unprecedented accuracy surpassing human specialists. Surgical robotic systems assist surgeons in conducting micro-invasive interventions with sub-millimeter precision. Concurrently, generative AI tools democratize creative writing and code development. However, ethicists caution that AI development must be strictly aligned with human values and safety standards.

801.readingText: The International Space Station (ISS) is a remarkable testament to peaceful international scientific cooperation. Flying approximately 400 kilometers above the Earth at a blistering orbital speed of 28,000 kilometers per hour, the football-field-sized laboratory circles our planet every 90 minutes. Since November 2000, rotating crews of international astronauts and cosmonauts have inhabited the station continuously, conducting pioneering investigations in microgravity physics, human biology, botany, and material sciences. Discoveries made aboard the ISS have contributed significantly to terrestrial medical treatments, water purification technologies, and advanced solar cells. Furthermore, the station serves as a crucial testing ground for physiological countermeasures required for future multi-year human expeditions to the Moon and Mars.

802.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Minh:: Do you believe humans will discover extraterrestrial microbial life on Mars, Phong?
Phong:: Scientists say that robotic rovers on Mars have detected subsurface water and organic compounds, so microbial existence might be plausible.
Minh:: How will technological inventions reshape our everyday communication in fifty years?
Phong:: We might communicate via real-time three-dimensional holographic projections instead of handheld video screens.
Minh:: Will language barriers completely dissolve?
Phong:: Certainly! Implantable neural translation earbuds will translate spoken languages instantaneously into your native tongue.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Artificial intelligence and autonomous robotic systems are ushering in the Fourth Industrial Revolution, fundamentally transforming healthcare, manufacturing, and exploratory science. In cutting-edge hospitals, machine-learning algorithms analyze radiological scans to detect early-stage malignant tumors with unprecedented accuracy surpassing human specialists. Surgical robotic systems assist surgeons in conducting micro-invasive interventions with sub-millimeter precision. Concurrently, generative AI tools democratize creative writing and code development. However, ethicists caution that AI development must be strictly aligned with human values and safety standards.

803.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Minh:: Do you believe humans will discover extraterrestrial microbial life on Mars, Phong?
Phong:: Scientists say that robotic rovers on Mars have detected subsurface water and organic compounds, so microbial existence might be plausible.
Minh:: How will technological inventions reshape our everyday communication in fifty years?
Phong:: We might communicate via real-time three-dimensional holographic projections instead of handheld video screens.
Minh:: Will language barriers completely dissolve?
Phong:: Certainly! Implantable neural translation earbuds will translate spoken languages instantaneously into your native tongue.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Artificial intelligence and autonomous robotic systems are ushering in the Fourth Industrial Revolution, fundamentally transforming healthcare, manufacturing, and exploratory science. In cutting-edge hospitals, machine-learning algorithms analyze radiological scans to detect early-stage malignant tumors with unprecedented accuracy surpassing human specialists. Surgical robotic systems assist surgeons in conducting micro-invasive interventions with sub-millimeter precision. Concurrently, generative AI tools democratize creative writing and code development. However, ethicists caution that AI development must be strictly aligned with human values and safety standards.

803.readingText: The International Space Station (ISS) is a remarkable testament to peaceful international scientific cooperation. Flying approximately 400 kilometers above the Earth at a blistering orbital speed of 28,000 kilometers per hour, the football-field-sized laboratory circles our planet every 90 minutes. Since November 2000, rotating crews of international astronauts and cosmonauts have inhabited the station continuously, conducting pioneering investigations in microgravity physics, human biology, botany, and material sciences. Discoveries made aboard the ISS have contributed significantly to terrestrial medical treatments, water purification technologies, and advanced solar cells. Furthermore, the station serves as a crucial testing ground for physiological countermeasures required for future multi-year human expeditions to the Moon and Mars.

=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Minh:: Do you believe humans will discover extraterrestrial microbial life on Mars, Phong?
Phong:: Scientists say that robotic rovers on Mars have detected subsurface water and organic compounds, so microbial existence might be plausible.
Minh:: How will technological inventions reshape our everyday communication in fifty years?
Phong:: We might communicate via real-time three-dimensional holographic projections instead of handheld video screens.
Minh:: Will language barriers completely dissolve?
Phong:: Certainly! Implantable neural translation earbuds will translate spoken languages instantaneously into your native tongue.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Artificial intelligence and autonomous robotic systems are ushering in the Fourth Industrial Revolution, fundamentally transforming healthcare, manufacturing, and exploratory science. In cutting-edge hospitals, machine-learning algorithms analyze radiological scans to detect early-stage malignant tumors with unprecedented accuracy surpassing human specialists. Surgical robotic systems assist surgeons in conducting micro-invasive interventions with sub-millimeter precision. Concurrently, generative AI tools democratize creative writing and code development. However, ethicists caution that AI development must be strictly aligned with human values and safety standards.

805.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Minh:: Do you believe humans will discover extraterrestrial microbial life on Mars, Phong?
Phong:: Scientists say that robotic rovers on Mars have detected subsurface water and organic compounds, so microbial existence might be plausible.
Minh:: How will technological inventions reshape our everyday communication in fifty years?
Phong:: We might communicate via real-time three-dimensional holographic projections instead of handheld video screens.
Minh:: Will language barriers completely dissolve?
Phong:: Certainly! Implantable neural translation earbuds will translate spoken languages instantaneously into your native tongue.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
Artificial intelligence and autonomous robotic systems are ushering in the Fourth Industrial Revolution, fundamentally transforming healthcare, manufacturing, and exploratory science. In cutting-edge hospitals, machine-learning algorithms analyze radiological scans to detect early-stage malignant tumors with unprecedented accuracy surpassing human specialists. Surgical robotic systems assist surgeons in conducting micro-invasive interventions with sub-millimeter precision. Concurrently, generative AI tools democratize creative writing and code development. However, ethicists caution that AI development must be strictly aligned with human values and safety standards.

Flying approximately 400 kilometers above the Earth at a blistering orbital speed of 28,000 kilometers per hour, the football-field-sized laboratory circles our planet every 90 minutes.
